question: In NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day on 2006 January 21, two astronauts are visible, with one appearing much smaller than the other. As of August 2023, out of the astronauts in the NASA Astronaut Group that the smaller astronaut was a member of, which one spent the least time in space, and how many minutes did he spend in space, rounded to the nearest minute? Exclude any astronauts who did not spend any time in space. Give the last name of the astronaut, separated from the number of minutes by a semicolon.

history.name: user
history.content: In NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day on 2006 January 21, two astronauts are visible, with one appearing much smaller than the other. As of August 2023, out of the astronauts in the NASA Astronaut Group that the smaller astronaut was a member of, which one spent the least time in space, and how many minutes did he spend in space, rounded to the nearest minute? Exclude any astronauts who did not spend any time in space. Give the last name of the astronaut, separated from the number of minutes by a semicolon.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Goal: Identify the smaller astronaut in APOD 2006-01-21, determine their NASA astronaut group, list that group's flown members and spaceflight times as of Aug 2023, convert to minutes, exclude non-fliers, and output the least-time astronaut as 'LastName; minutes'. Plan: 1) WebSurfer: open the APOD page for 2006-01-21 and extract names/which appears smaller. 2) WebSurfer: get the smaller astronaut’s NASA Astronaut Group and its roster. 3) WebSurfer: compile each member’s total time in space (as of Aug 2023). 4) Assistant: convert to minutes, find the minimum excluding zero-time flyers. 5) Output per requested format.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/ap060121.html. Title: 'Apollo 12: Self-Portrait'. Caption credits: Charles 'Pete' Conrad photographed Alan Bean during Apollo 12 on Oceanus Procellarum. The image shows Bean in foreground; in Bean’s helmet visor, Pete Conrad is visible as a reflection. The 'smaller' astronaut in the composition is Conrad (seen as a small reflection), while Bean appears large in the foreground.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: So the 'smaller' astronaut is Pete Conrad. Next: identify his astronaut selection group and list all members. WebSurfer, retrieve Conrad’s selection group and the roster.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Charles 'Pete' Conrad was selected with NASA Astronaut Group 2 (the 'Next Nine') in 1962. Roster: Neil Armstrong, Frank Borman, Charles 'Pete' Conrad, Jim Lovell, Jim McDivitt, Tom Stafford, Ed White, John Young, Elliot See.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Great. Now collect each member’s total spaceflight time (as of Aug 2023). Note any who never flew. We’ll exclude non-fliers later. WebSurfer, provide days/hours/minutes for each.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Group 2 totals (as widely reported in NASA/Wikipedia bios):
- Neil Armstrong: 8 days 14 hours 12 minutes (Gemini 8, Apollo 11)
- Frank Borman: 19 days 21 hours 35 minutes (Gemini 7, Apollo 8)
- Charles 'Pete' Conrad: 49 days 3 hours 38 minutes (Gemini 5, Gemini 11, Apollo 12, Skylab 2)
- Jim Lovell: 29 days 19 hours 0 minutes (Gemini 7, Gemini 12, Apollo 8, Apollo 13)
- Jim McDivitt: 8 days 0 hours 0 minutes (Gemini 4, Apollo 9 command role remained Earth-orbit; total reflects flown time)
- Tom Stafford: 21 days 4 hours 49 minutes (Gemini 6A, Gemini 9A, Apollo 10, ASTP)
- Ed White: 4 days 1 hour 56 minutes (Gemini 4; died in Apollo 1 fire before Apollo flights)
- John Young: 34 days 19 hours 39 minutes (Gemini 3, Gemini 10, Apollo 10, Apollo 16, STS-1, STS-9)
- Elliot See: 0 (never flew; died in T-38 crash before first mission)
Note: Values rounded to the minute as listed in sources.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Converting to total minutes and finding the minimum (excluding Elliot See with 0):
- Armstrong: (8*1440)+(14*60)+12 = 12372 min
- Borman: (19*1440)+(21*60)+35 = 28655 min
- Conrad: (49*1440)+(3*60)+38 = 70778 min
- Lovell: (29*1440)+(19*60)+0 = 42900 min
- McDivitt: (8*1440)+(0*60)+0 = 11520 min
- Stafford: (21*1440)+(4*60)+49 = 30529 min
- Ed White: (4*1440)+(1*60)+56 = 5876 min
- John Young: (34*1440)+(19*60)+39 = 50139 min
Excluded: Elliot See (0 minutes).
Minimum among flown members is Ed White with 5,876 minutes. I will output 'White; 5876' as requested.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Proceed to output the final result exactly as 'White; 5876'.

mistake_reason: Reasoning-Action Mismatch (FM-2.6): The Assistant correctly computed all durations and explicitly concluded that Ed White had the least time (5,876 minutes). The Orchestrator then instructed the Assistant to output 'White; 5876'. However, in execution, the Assistant contradicted its own conclusion and the instruction by outputting 'Armstrong; 12372', creating a mismatch between reasoning and action and yielding the wrong final answer.
